words.sense: not belonging to or proper to a thing; external; non-essential
words.connotation: Negative; implies removal is an improvement.

words.sense: not contained in or forming an essential part of something; acting from outside
words.concise_meaning: Coming from an external source, often contrasting with internal.

semantic_axes.description: Whether the element is superfluous (extraneous) versus a necessary part of the whole's external structure (extrinsic).
extraneous focuses on lack of utility; extrinsic focuses on external origin.

edge.boundary_rule: If it's just 'added junk' that could be removed without consequence, use 'extraneous'. If it's a 'necessary external component or influence', use 'extrinsic'.

misconceptions.M2: Thinking 'extrinsic' means something extra that should be thrown away.
misconceptions.M3: Ignoring the requirement of an element to the system.

extraneous: The professor asked us to cut all extraneous details from the report.
The article was filled with extraneous anecdotes that added nothing.
To focus on the experiment, they removed all extraneous noise.
His speech was too long because of all the extraneous commentary.
The editor removed the extraneous chapters that stalled the plot.
Delete any extraneous variables that don't affect the final result.
extrinsic: Her dedication was driven by extrinsic motivation, like bonuses.
Extrinsic factors like the economy influenced the company's growth.
The extrinsic value of the house is higher than its intrinsic charm.
The pressure to succeed was an extrinsic force she had to manage.
The design's beauty is extrinsic to its actual function.
Unlike internal drive, extrinsic rewards are only temporary.

extraneous: The company's success was largely extraneous to its core strategy.
He found it hard to ignore the extraneous rewards of his job.
The building's height is extraneous to its structural stability.
She focused on the extraneous factors of her health, like diet.
The team ignored the extraneous input from the CEO.
We need to consider the extrinsic benefits, not just internal ones.
extrinsic: Please remove these extrinsic paragraphs from your essay.
The story was ruined by too many extrinsic, unnecessary details.
She spent hours deleting extrinsic data from the spreadsheet.
The speaker's extrinsic comments made everyone feel bored.
There is too much extrinsic jargon in this technical manual.
The teacher asked him to stop making extrinsic interruptions.

borderline.text: The project's success depended on [word] factors like team bonuses.
borderline.note: Bonuses are a necessary external motivation, not just unnecessary junk.

borderline.text: I tried to ignore the [word] advice that had nothing to do with my goal.
The [word] parts of the machine, like the outer cover, are just for protection.
borderline.note: They are external, but functional, not 'junk'.

borderline.text: She cleaned her desk by removing all [word] papers.

chains.frame: What the student added to the essay: ___

beats.text: The student included a long paragraph about the history of pencils.
beats.decisive_clue: long paragraph about history of pencils
beats.reason: It's unnecessary information for the essay.

beats.text: The essay is about modern architecture, and that history paragraph makes the word count way too high.
beats.decisive_clue: makes the word count too high
beats.reason: It clutter the essay and serves no purpose.

chains.feedback_short: The paragraph is unnecessary clutter, making it extraneous.
chains.feedback_deep: The information about pencil history is completely irrelevant to an essay on modern architecture, and it actually hurts the essay by bloating the word count. Therefore, it is extraneous.
chains.contrast_rule: Unnecessary junk is extraneous; necessary external factors are extrinsic.
chains.hint: Does it help the essay or just take up space?

chains.frame: The reason for Elena's motivation: ___

beats.text: Elena works hard to get her end-of-year bonus.
beats.reason: It is an external factor acting as motivation.

beats.text: She doesn't really care about the project itself, she just wants that cash.
beats.reason: It reinforces the external nature of the motivation.

chains.feedback_short: The bonus is an external factor, so the motivation is extrinsic.
chains.feedback_deep: The bonus is an external incentive, not something arising from Elena's internal passion for the project. Thus, it is extrinsic motivation.
chains.contrast_rule: Motivation from external rewards is extrinsic.
chains.hint: Is the drive coming from inside or outside?

chains.frame: The influence of Sarah's parents on her marriage: ___

beats.text: Sarah's parents pay for her and her husband's apartment.
beats.reason: It is an external factor supporting their life.

beats.text: While nice, it creates a dynamic where the couple feels obligated to listen to their advice.
beats.reason: The financial support is an external, structural factor in the marriage.

chains.feedback_short: This support is a necessary external factor, hence extrinsic.
chains.feedback_deep: The financial support is an external, structural component impacting the relationship, not useless junk, making it extrinsic, not extraneous.
chains.hint: Is the support a necessary part of their life structure?

chains.frame: The decoration on the frame: ___

beats.text: The artist added glitter to the frame.
It completely hides the original wood texture, which was the point of the piece.
beats.reason: It is clearly unnecessary and negative.

chains.feedback_short: The glitter distracts and adds nothing, so it is extraneous.
chains.feedback_deep: The glitter is unnecessary and actually detracts from the art piece's intended effect, so it is extraneous clutter.
chains.hint: Does it add value or just clutter?

chains.frame: The impact of inflation on the business: ___

beats.text: Inflation raised the cost of raw materials for the company.
Even though they managed their internal costs well, they couldn't control this external price hike.
beats.decisive_clue: couldn't control this external price hike

chains.feedback_short: Inflation is an external, necessary factor for the business to manage.
chains.feedback_deep: Inflation is an external economic force, not unnecessary noise, so it is an extrinsic factor.
chains.contrast_rule: Factors arising from outside are extrinsic.
chains.hint: Is inflation something that can be ignored or something that must be accounted for?

chains.frame: The effect of the slides on the talk: ___

beats.text: The speaker used animations on every slide.
The audience spent more time trying to figure out the animations than listening to the speaker.

chains.feedback_short: The animations are clutter that distract from the main message.
chains.feedback_deep: The animations serve no constructive purpose and distract the audience, making them extraneous clutter.
chains.hint: Does the audience need the animations to understand the message?

chains.frame: The reason the team lost: ___

beats.text: The coach spent all week talking about the fans' reactions.
beats.reason: Focusing on that didn't help the game plan.

beats.text: Actually, the noise levels in the stadium were a key environmental factor in their communication breakdown.
beats.reason: It's an external, structural factor in the game.

chains.feedback_short: Initially it was a distraction, but it turned out to be a key structural factor.
chains.feedback_deep: At first, the focus on fans seemed like unnecessary talk (extraneous). Later, it became clear the stadium noise itself was a major external factor influencing the game (extrinsic).
chains.contrast_rule: Distractions are extraneous; essential external conditions are extrinsic.
chains.hint: Does it just distract, or is it a structural condition?

chains.frame: The packing choices: ___

beats.text: He packed a bulky tuxedo for his backpacking trip.
He had to pack it because the local law required formal attire for certain temple visits.
beats.reason: It's an external requirement, not just junk.

chains.feedback_short: It's a requirement of the environment, not just junk.
chains.feedback_deep: The tuxedo initially seemed like junk (extraneous), but because the law required it, it became a necessary external factor (extrinsic).
chains.hint: Why does he have to pack it?

chains.frame: The items left on the counter: ___

beats.text: Sarah keeps an old, broken toy on the kitchen counter.
She actually needs it there because its sensor activates the automatic cabinet light.

chains.feedback_short: It serves a technical function, so it's a necessary external component.
chains.feedback_deep: The toy looked like junk (extraneous), but it serves a technical purpose to activate a light (extrinsic structural component).
chains.contrast_rule: Useless junk is extraneous; functional external components are extrinsic.
chains.hint: Does the toy actually *do* anything?

chains.frame: The consultant's approach: ___

beats.text: The consultant added five new, complex software tools to the team's process.
Actually, the new compliance laws make these tools essential for reporting.

chains.feedback_short: The software is a necessary external requirement.
chains.feedback_deep: The tools seemed like unnecessary complication (extraneous) until it was revealed they are required by law (extrinsic factor).
chains.hint: Why are the tools being added?

chains.frame: The feedback the teacher gave: ___

beats.text: The teacher told the student to ignore the grammar exercises.
The student needs to master writing flow, which is a different skill, not dependent on the grammar rules.
beats.decisive_clue: different skill, not dependent on grammar

chains.feedback_short: Grammar is an external skill, separate from writing flow.
chains.feedback_deep: Grammar is an external set of rules (extrinsic to writing flow). The teacher meant they are separate skills, not 'junk'.
chains.hint: Are the exercises junk or just a different, external skill?

chains.frame: The background color of the painting: ___

beats.text: The artist chose a bright pink background for a funeral portrait.
beats.decisive_clue: bright pink for a funeral portrait

beats.text: The portrait was commissioned by the deceased to highlight his vibrant life.
beats.decisive_clue: commissioned by the deceased to highlight his life
beats.reason: The commission is an external requirement.

chains.feedback_short: The background was a necessary request, not just a mistake.
chains.feedback_deep: Initially it seemed like an unnecessary mistake (extraneous). But the commission requirement (an external factor) made it necessary (extrinsic).
chains.hint: Why did the artist choose that color?

chains.frame: The reason for the company's low stock price: ___

beats.text: The company's stock fell, even though its internal profits are record-breaking.
The entire sector is down due to a new trade policy.
beats.decisive_clue: entire sector is down due to trade policy

chains.feedback_short: It narrows down the external factor to a specific policy.
chains.feedback_deep: It was already clearly an extrinsic factor, but the new info clarifies that it's specifically trade policy. Still extrinsic, just more precise.
chains.hint: Is it about internal or external issues?

chains.frame: The reason the test was difficult: ___

beats.text: The test featured questions that were completely off-topic.
They were about pop culture rather than the math we studied.
beats.decisive_clue: about pop culture rather than math
beats.reason: They clearly don't belong in a math test.

chains.feedback_short: They are just clutter.
chains.feedback_deep: The questions were already extraneous, and knowing they are about pop culture just confirms they are even more irrelevant.
chains.hint: Why are these questions irrelevant?

chains.frame: The reason for the manager's unhappiness: ___

beats.text: The manager is frustrated with the team's progress.
It's because the client keeps changing the requirements.
beats.reason: Client needs are an external structural factor.

chains.feedback_short: Client demands are a necessary external factor.
chains.feedback_deep: Client requirements are an external structural element for the team's work, not junk, making them extrinsic.
chains.contrast_rule: Client requirements are an extrinsic factor.
chains.hint: Is the issue the team itself or an external force?

chains.frame: The sculptor's decision to add clay: ___

beats.text: The sculptor added more clay to the torso.
It makes it easier to support the arm's weight.

chains.feedback_short: It's still structural, so extrinsic remains correct.
chains.feedback_deep: The added clay was and is a necessary structural element, so extrinsic remains correct throughout.
chains.hint: Does it add structural integrity?

chains.frame: The reason for the audience's boredom: ___

beats.text: The speaker kept reading from a dense, tiny-font script.
He didn't need the script at all, as he was an expert on the topic.
beats.decisive_clue: didn't need the script at all

chains.feedback_short: The script was unnecessary clutter, so extraneous remains correct.
chains.feedback_deep: The script was just unnecessary clutter from the start, and knowing it wasn't needed confirms it was extraneous.
chains.hint: Does he need the script to speak?

chains.frame: The reason the student is reading extra books: ___

beats.text: The student reads books not on the syllabus.
Wait, those books are essential for a special scholarship requirement.
beats.decisive_clue: essential for a special scholarship requirement
beats.reason: Now it's an external structural requirement.

chains.feedback_short: It's a necessary external factor.
chains.feedback_deep: They first seemed like unnecessary reading (extraneous). But the scholarship requirement is a necessary external factor (extrinsic), reframing the action.
chains.hint: Why are they reading the books?

chains.frame: The reason for adding the security check: ___

beats.text: The office added a new digital check-in system.
The IT guy just installed it to show off his own coding project.
beats.decisive_clue: show off his own coding project
beats.reason: It's just for his ego, not for security.

chains.feedback_short: It was structural, then revealed to be just unnecessary noise.
chains.feedback_deep: The system seemed like a legitimate structural change (extrinsic). But learning it was just for the IT guy's ego makes it unnecessary, extraneous noise.
chains.hint: What is the true reason for the addition?

chains.frame: The reason for the professor's strict grading of the formatting: ___

beats.text: The professor takes off points if the margin is off by a millimeter.
He argues that attention to strict, formal structural constraints is necessary for academic precision.
beats.reason: Confirms the structural, external nature of the rule.

chains.feedback_short: Formatting rules are a structural, external constraint.
chains.feedback_deep: Formatting rules are a necessary external structural constraint, hence extrinsic, not useless clutter.
chains.hint: Is formatting junk or a structural constraint?
